clue.text: Incredibly cheap drinks for supporters in skirts

parts.note: a farthing was the old British quarter-penny, so anything worth a farthing is extremely cheap
ales are drinks of beer

explanation.surface: Someone runs a bargain bar offering bottom-price drinks to the backers of skirt-wearers.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHING was the smallest British coin, a quarter of an old penny, hence 'incredibly cheap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooped frames worn under Tudor dresses held the fabric out, so they were the supports beneath a skirt.

clue.text: Dishonestly obtain data about horse

indicators.note: about means going round, so the data word is wrapped around the horse word

parts.note: a file is a body of stored data
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Someone cheats to get information about a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle something by trickery or deceit is to get it dishonestly.

clue.text: Peers are possessed by this field of study

definitions.meaning: lords are peers of the kingdom, which in that phrase belongs to them
a domain or sphere of knowledge

explanation.definitionFit: Peers of the kingdom belong to a domain, and a domain is also a sphere of knowledge.

clue.text: Knock on gate to get out?

definitions.text: Knock on gate to get out?

parts.words: Knock on gate to get out?
parts.note: read as cricket: striking the stumps (a gate is another word for them) with your own bat is a way to be dismissed

explanation.surface: Someone raps on a gate in order to be let out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out if they knock the stumps with bat or body; 'out' is the cricket dismissal, not leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket dismissal happens when a batter strikes their own stumps, a knock on the wicket.

clue.text: Secure northern beer, when told

indicators.note: when told means spoken out, so the letters are heard rather than read

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern, and ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone orders a northern ale over the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something firmly with a spike is to make it secure.

clue.text: Degree one didn't turn up to receive

definitions.text: Degree one didn't turn up to receive

parts.words: Degree one didn't turn up to receive
parts.note: a university award granted to a student too ill to sit the final exams

explanation.surface: A graduate skips the ceremony for their own degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is 'didn't turn up': not missing the graduation, but missing the exams through illness.
explanation.definitionFit: British universities grant this unclassified pass to a candidate certified as sick during finals.

clue.text: Oiled, or became less tight

explanation.definitionFit: Lubricating a joint makes it slide freely, and a loosening grip also slackens.

clue.text: Tree found by river in north of Devon

parts.note: the Tamar is the river forming the Devon-Cornwall border

indicators.note: north of a down entry means its top letter, the first of Devon

explanation.surface: A tree is spotted beside a river in the north of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical leguminous tree bearing sour pods used in cooking.

clue.text: Cheat to avoid church

parts.note: to flee is to run away from, avoid
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone skips church services to swindle others.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle or rob them, as a sheep is shorn.

clue.text: New conductor's function almost a disaster

parts.note: a lightning conductor works by earthing the electrical charge

explanation.surface: A new orchestral conductor's concert nearly turns into a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra; it is an electrical conductor, whose job is earthing.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape, a disaster only just avoided.

clue.text: Booth's seat in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a small stand at a market or fair
a seat on the ground floor of a theatre, in the front

explanation.definitionFit: A market booth is a stand selling goods, and front ground-floor theatre seats bear the same name.

clue.text: Opening carriage occupied by doctor

indicators.note: occupied by means the carriage word holds the doctor word within it

parts.note: carriage is the way one walks or holds oneself, one's gait
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor is sitting in a carriage at the start of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle; it means bearing or gait.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess move sacrificing material at the start of a game, so an opening ploy.

clue.text: Thick characters showing brazen impudence

definitions.meaning: heavy dark type used for emphasis in printing

explanation.definitionFit: Heavy type is printed in dark strokes, and a shameless expression is the same phrase for effrontery.

clue.text: Bather's cry when noticing water rising?

definitions.text: Bather's cry when noticing water rising?

parts.words: Bather's cry when noticing water rising?
parts.note: the legendary shout of Archimedes in his bath on seeing the water level go up as he got in

explanation.surface: Someone in the tub yells as the bathwater climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Archimedes is said to have shouted this Greek 'I have found it' on discovering displacement in his bath.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek exclamation of discovery is what Archimedes cried on realising displacement.

clue.text: Clothing business distributing garter ad

indicators.note: distributing means the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion firm hands out an advert for garters.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal name for the fashion and garment industry.

clue.text: Confident, or ruddy hopeful?

explanation.definitionFit: The word means optimistic in temperament and also blood-red in complexion.

clue.text: Burrowing animal could be selfish user of land

definitions.meaning: the North American woodchuck, which digs burrows

definitions.text: could be selfish user of land
definitions.meaning: a hog is a greedy person, so one hogging the soil

explanation.definitionFit: The woodchuck digs burrows, and a hog of the earth would be greedy about land.

clue.text: Recent arrival of Nemo and crew at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Captain Nemo and his crew are aboard the Nautilus out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has just arrived or joined.

clue.text: Generator, for example, needs improved casing

indicators.note: casing means the improved word forms a shell around the example word

parts.note: better means improved

explanation.surface: A power generator needs a better housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generator' looks like a machine; it means one who fathers or originates.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fathers or produces something, an originator.

clue.text: North African prickly shrub is eradicated

indicators.note: eradicated means wiped out, so the letters of is are removed

parts.note: berberis is the spiny barberry shrub

explanation.surface: A thorny bush in North Africa is uprooted.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the indigenous Amazigh peoples of North Africa.

clue.text: Exhibit type of jam

explanation.definitionFit: Displaying something is lifting it into view, and a traffic delay has the same name.

clue.text: Joke about girl being narrow-minded

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joke word goes round the girl

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A joke about a girl is called small-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and prudish in morals, puritanical.

clue.text: In conversation, bring up rodents and bats

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the letters come from speech

parts.note: to rear mice is to bring up rodents

explanation.surface: Someone mentions in chat raising rodents and bats.
explanation.walkthrough: An archaic word for bats, met mainly in crosswords and old poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic plural name for flying mammals of the night.

clue.text: Precocious girl, or woman, embraced by males

indicators.note: embraced by means held between, so the woman sits inside the males

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so two males give two Ms
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A forward girl, or a woman, is hugged by men.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky, presumptuous young girl, as in 'little minx'.

clue.text: I may do casting, having one settled as English king

parts.note: the Angles settled in England and gave it its name
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: An actor in casting settles as an English king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' suggests a film audition; it is casting a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisher casts a line, so is one who does casting.

clue.text: Desert holiday

definitions.meaning: to abandon or go away from

explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning a place is going away from it, and time off work is also permission to be away.

clue.text: Exam taken, as the Georgics were long ago omitted

indicators.note: omitted means the long ago word is left out

parts.note: Virgil's Georgics are poems of rural life, pastoral poetry
past means long ago

explanation.surface: An exam is set on how Virgil's farming poems were once left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's Georgics are Latin poems on farming and country life.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as opposed to a written one.

clue.text: Losing wife, went and died

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the wife letter is taken away

parts.note: wended means went, made one's way

explanation.surface: A widower lost his wife, wandered off and passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to an end, finished, like a life.

clue.text: Month spent producing ceremonial parade

parts.note: March is a month
past means spent or gone by

explanation.surface: A month is used up preparing a ceremonial parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal procession of troops past a saluting dignitary.

clue.text: Jewel that one may be putting on to provide colour

parts.note: an emerald is a jewel

parts.words: that one may be putting on
parts.note: in golf, putting is done on the green

explanation.surface: A jewel someone might be wearing supplies colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on' suggests wearing; it is putting in golf, done on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright, vivid shade like the gemstone.
